review_method: Independent cold review of the packet, its actual sealed subject inputs, registered source metadata and exact available source evidence. No reliance on another reviewer verdict. No source changes or workflow advancement.

consequential_difficulty_test.question: Does the three-measures image warrant the two readings or a proof of the Trinity?
consequential_difficulty_test.loci: Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew46.2; Jerome, Commentary on MatthewII on13:33, PL26cols91–92
consequential_difficulty_test.outcome: Pass: Chrysostom explains much meal and contact; Jerome offers comprehensive human transformation and explicitly refuses dogmatic proof from uncertain parables. The proposal preserves the difference and treats its Trinity-Preface connection as synthesis.

consequential_difficulty_test.question: Can confidence in deliverance coexist with affliction, and does ask-anything promise arbitrary temporal success?
consequential_difficulty_test.loci: Chrysostom, First Thessalonians1 on1:4–6; Augustine, Enarratio129.1–8; Bede, Mark11:22–25 neighborhood; SchusterIII188–189
consequential_difficulty_test.outcome: Pass: the actual sources distinguish bodily trial from Spirit-given joy, ground hope in Christ, and connect prayer to pardon, charity and eternal life. The proposed readings retain those constraints.

chronology.result: No substantive defect found in the qualified selected traditional proposals. Composition and narrated-event claims remain distinct; Korahite range is a collection bound, Psalm occasions remain unresolved in full evidence, and possible Davidic attribution remains conditional. Compact ranges follow the later chronology orientation guidance and do not assert unique consensus dates.

source_reconciliation.result: No unsupported new admission found. Concrete deferrals preserve natural extent, language, transcription and rights limitations. All reviewed source identities are exact; the one controlling rights inventory omission remains blocking.

limits: This is a bounded research review, not an exhaustive reading of every author or historical volume.
Original Greek was not consulted for NPNF translations; rights-limited modern Aquinas delivery supports attributed paraphrase, not a new purported historical English quotation.
Chronology checks test the retained traditional proposals and their qualifications, not contemporary scholarly consensus.
The Google rights inventory was read to establish the dependency omission; it is not part of the current sealed inputs. This review does not make a fresh legal ruling.
No downstream study, concise study, homily or rendered publication was reviewed at this stage.
